questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Quadratic Equations and Inequalities
questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={k\in Z:{k}^{2}+1\le 5}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality ${k}^{2}+1\le 5.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{k}^{2}+1 & \le 5 \\ {k}^{2} & \le 4 \\ \sqrt{{k}^{2}} & \le \sqrt{4} \\ |k| & \le 2 \\ -2\le k & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the inequality above are $0,\pm 1,\pm 2.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A={0,\pm 1,\pm 2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Quadratic Equations and Inequalities
questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:{x}^{2}+1=0}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation ${x}^{2}+1=0.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+1 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =-1 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{-1} \\ x & =\pm \text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

However, since $x\in R$ and $\pm \text{i}\notin R,$ we conclude that the set $A$ contains no elements. Hence, $A=∅.$

questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in N:|\frac{n}{4}|=3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the equation $|\frac{n}{4}|=3.$ So, we first need to solve for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\frac{n}{4}| & =3 \\ \frac{n}{4} & =\pm 3 \\ n & =\pm 12 \\ n & =-12,12\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $n=-12$ and $n=12.$ However, since $-12\notin N,$ we conclude that the set $A$ contains only one element, namely $n=12.$

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={12}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)=1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)=1
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\pi x & =2n\pi  \\ x & =2n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm 2,\,\pm 4,\,\pm 6,\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\,\pm 2,\,\pm 4,\,\pm 6,\,…}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)=-1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi x)=-1
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi x & =\pi +2n\pi  \\ 2x & =1+2n \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}+n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,\pm \frac{5}{2},\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,\pm \frac{5}{2},\,…}.
$$
